evidence.quote: The resultant microstructure is one of smaller, equiaxed γ-grains away from the prior β-grain boundaries, with coarser primary γ-laths which formed at that interface.

Evidence of this transformation behavior can be seen in the aged microstructures of 15Nb and 20Nb alloys by observing differences between γ-phase morphology near and away from the prior β-grain boundaries. Near these boundaries a coarser acicular morphology is seen, while away from them a very fine structure is observed, as illustrated in Figure 7.

mechanisms.name: competitive nucleation of γ and σ from β phase

evidence.quote: Since both γ- and σ-phases only nucleate from β phase [27, 33], each one’s presence limits the potential nucleation and growth of the other since they will preferentially nucleate at the interface the other has with β -phase [21, 27].

It has been observed [30, 33] that γ-phase precipitates quickly from the prior β -phase grain boundaries, in a widmanstatten morphology that can occur upon quenching or early in subsequent heating during aging.
It has been observed in samples of 15Nb alloy subjected to less severe quench that γ-phase will continue to grow into large laths if unhindered, as shown in Figure 8.
The resultant microstructure is one of smaller, equiaxed γ-grains away from the prior β-grain boundaries, with coarser primary γ-laths which formed at that interface.

Evidence of this transformation behavior can be seen in the aged microstructures of 15Nb and 20Nb alloys by observing differences between γ-phase morphology near and away from the prior β-grain boundaries. Near these boundaries a coarser acicular morphology is seen, while away from them a very fine structure is observed, as illustrated in Figure 7.
with an increase to 25 at% Nb, aged microstructures transition to a coarser microstructure with more connected σ-phase due to γ-phase formation upon quenching.
The precipitation of σ-phase inhibits the coarsening of γ-laths as well as provides additional nucleation sites for γ.
If σ-phase nucleates first or concurrently with the γ-phase, only the remaining β between σ-phase particles can transform to γ-phase, producing a very fine equiaxed microstructure.
It has been demonstrated that the addition of 5at% Cr to a high-Nb TiAlNb alloy significantly stabilizes the β -phase and allows for the retention of β -phase to room temperature upon quenching [21].

increasing Nb increases phase transformation temperatures for equilibrium phase transformations, suppresses metastable (β → γ+σ ) transformation temperatures, increases γ-TiAl formation during quench, as Nb stabilizes all phases to higher temperature, and increases phase fraction of Nb-rich σ-phase.
